questions.question: Which description fits a linear program (LP)?
options: A linear objective, made large or small, under constraints that must all be of the form $\le$
A linear objective, made large or small, with every variable restricted to whole numbers
A linear objective, made large or small, under linear equality or inequality constraints
Any objective, made large or small, as long as each constraint is a linear inequality

questions.question: In an LP whose variables have no integer restrictions, may a variable take the value 2.5 in a solution?
options: Yes; LP variables are continuous unless restricted
No; LP variables are whole numbers by default
No; fractions are rounded before reporting a plan
Only if the objective coefficient is also a fraction

questions.question: A model makes $z=4x_1-2x_2$ as large as possible subject to linear constraints. Does the negative coefficient $-2$ stop it from being an LP?
options: Yes; LP coefficients must all be positive numbers
Yes; a negative coefficient makes the term nonlinear
No; negative coefficients are fully allowed in an LP
No, but only if $-2$ appears in no constraint as well

questions.question: Why do OR models so often keep the objective and constraints linear?
options: Real costs and capacities are always exactly linear in practice
Nonlinear models cannot be solved at all, only approximated
Linear models can be solved efficiently, even large ones
Linear models give whole-number plans, which practice needs

questions.question: Must every linear program be written as a maximization with only $\le$ constraints?
options: Yes; that form is part of the definition of a linear program
No, but equalities are not allowed in a linear program
No, but $\ge$ constraints are allowed only when minimizing
No; $\ge$, equalities and minimization are allowed as well

questions.question: Which of these constraints on decision variables $x_1,x_2$ is linear and may appear in an LP?
options: $\sqrt{x_1}+x_2\le3$

questions.question: An LP has constraints $\sum_{j=1}^{4}a_{ij}x_j\le b_i$ for $i=1,\dots,3$. With $n$ the number of decision variables and $m$ the number of these constraints, what are $n$ and $m$?
Solve the LP: make $z=5x$ as large as possible subject to $2x\le7$ and $x\ge0$. What is the optimal $x$?
Which description of production cost for $x$ units gives a term that can appear in a linear objective?
options: 6 per unit plus 50 once if anything is made
6 per unit up to 100 units, then 4 per unit
6 times the square of the number of units
6 euros per unit, for any number of units

questions.question: Which of these models is a linear program, with $x_1,x_2$ continuous unless stated otherwise?
A revenue term $px$ appears in a model, where $x$ is the quantity sold. When is $px$ a linear term?
options: Always, since it has the form price times quantity
When $p$ is given data, not a decision variable
Never, since it is a product of two symbols
Only when $p$ is positive, whatever its role

questions.question: A model contains the constraint $4x_1+2\le3x_2+x_1$, where $x_1,x_2$ are decision variables. Is it a linear constraint?
options: No; variables on both sides make it nonlinear
No; a linear constraint has a constant on the right
Yes; collecting the terms gives $3x_1-3x_2\le-2$
Yes, but only after multiplying both sides by $x_2$

questions.question: An LP decides how many buses $x$ to run, and its best plan has $x=12.4$. What does this show about modelling indivisible decisions with an LP?
options: The LP has made an error, since buses are whole
A whole-number rule has to be stated explicitly
The meaning of $x$ already forces whole numbers
The objective will prevent fractional bus numbers

questions.question: Two ingredients cost 4 and 7 euros per kg; $x_1,x_2$ are the kg used, and $x_1+x_2>0$. The average cost per kg, $\frac{4x_1+7x_2}{x_1+x_2}$, may be at most 5. Which linear constraint is equivalent?
A model requires $|x_1-x_2|\le3$, where $x_1,x_2$ are decision variables. Which pair of linear constraints allows exactly the same plans?
options: $x_1-x_2\le3$ and nothing else
$x_1\le3$ and $x_2\le3$
$(x_1-x_2)^2\le9$ alone

questions.question: An LP makes $z=4x_1+3x_2-2x_3$ as large as possible subject to $x_1+x_2+x_3\le10$ and $x_1,x_2,x_3\ge0$. Which modification keeps it an LP?
options: Requiring $x_3$ to be a whole number
Adding the constraint $x_1\ge2x_2-7$
Replacing $-2x_3$ in $z$ by $-2x_3^2$
Adding the constraint $x_1x_2\ge1$

questions.question: A model has a linear objective and linear constraints, but no sign restrictions: its continuous variables may also take negative values. Is it a linear program?
options: Yes; sign restrictions are not part of the LP definition
No; an LP must contain $x_j\ge0$ for every variable
No; without sign restrictions it has no constraints
Yes, but only if all its constraints are of type $\le$

questions.question: A model has a linear objective and linear constraints, and additionally requires $x_1$ to be a whole number. Is it a linear program?
options: Yes; its objective and constraints are all linear
No; a whole-number rule makes the objective nonlinear
Yes, as a whole-number rule is a linear constraint
No; LP variables are continuous, and this one is not

questions.question: A model with continuous variables $x_1,x_2$ and no sign restrictions contains $(x_1+x_2)^2\le16$. Which linear constraints allow exactly the same plans?
options: $x_1\le4$ and $x_2\le4$

questions.question: A modeller replaces the constraint $\frac{x_1}{x_2}\le2$ by $x_1\le2x_2$, although $x_2$ may be negative. Which plan satisfies $x_1\le2x_2$ but violates $\frac{x_1}{x_2}\le2$?
